title: Building APIs
game_role: At the end of the game, your score is sent to your API.
objective: Design your own API: write functions that answer GET, POST, PUT and DELETE requests
story: The summit is very close! Yesterday we asked other stations questions; today **we** become the station that answers them. Your friends' games will be able to read the scores of Piko's Adventure from the API you write.

sections.title: HTTP methods
sections.body:
Every request that reaches an API has a **method**. The method says what should be done:

- `GET`: fetch data (read)
- `POST`: add new data
- `PUT`: update existing data
- `DELETE`: delete data

These four operations are called **CRUD** for short: Create, Read, Update, Delete.

sections.title: Addresses and IDs
sections.body:
API addresses are usually organized like this:

- `GET /players` all players
- `GET /players/2` the player with ID 2
- `POST /players` add a new player
- `DELETE /players/2` delete player number 2

`split` helps take an address apart: `"/players/2".split("/")` gives `['', 'players', '2']`

sections.title: A real API with Flask
sections.body:
```python
from flask import Flask, jsonify, request
app = Flask(__name__)
players = []

@app.route("/players", methods=["GET"])
def list_players():
    return jsonify(players), 200

@app.route("/players", methods=["POST"])
def create_player():
    data = request.get_json()
    players.append(data)
    return jsonify(data), 201
```

Without setting up a server, we'll build the same logic with plain functions: each function returns `(status_code, response)`.

sections.title: The right status code
sections.body:
- `200` OK (successful GET and PUT)
- `201` Created (successful POST)
- `204` No Content (successful DELETE)
- `400` Bad Request (missing information)
- `404` Not Found

A good API always returns a clear status code and error message.

tasks.title: GET: one player
tasks.prompt: If `get_player(pid)` finds the player with ID `pid`, it should return `(200, player)`; if not, `(404, {"error": "not found"})`.
tasks.starter:
players = [{"id": 1, "name": "Piko"}, {"id": 2, "name": "Emma"}]

def get_player(pid):
    pass

print(get_player(2))
print(get_player(7))
hints: Walk through the players; when the id matches, return 200, p
When the loop ends, return 404, {"error": "not found"}

tasks.title: POST: a new player
tasks.prompt:
`create_player(body)`:

- If `body` has no `name`, return `(400, {"error": "name required"})`.
- Otherwise add the new player as `{"id": next_number, "name": ...}` and return `(201, player)`. The next number is one more than the biggest ID.
tasks.starter:
players = [{"id": 1, "name": "Piko"}, {"id": 4, "name": "Emma"}]

def create_player(body):
    pass

print(create_player({"name": "Ben"}))
print(create_player({}))
hints: Check first: if "name" not in body:
The biggest ID: max([p["id"] for p in players])
max fails on an empty list; you can use max(..., default=0).

tasks.title: DELETE: remove a player
tasks.prompt: If `delete_player(pid)` finds and deletes the player, it should return `(204, None)`; if not, `(404, {"error": "not found"})`.
tasks.starter:
players = [{"id": 1, "name": "Piko"}, {"id": 2, "name": "Emma"}]

def delete_player(pid):

print(delete_player(1))
print(players)
hints: When you find the player: players.remove(p)

challenge.title: Router
challenge.prompt:
`handle(method, path, body=None)` should send each request to the right function:

- `GET /players`: `(200, players)`
- `GET /players/2`: `get_player(2)`
- `POST /players`: `create_player(body)`
- Everything else: `(404, {"error": "no such path"})`
hints: Decide by the number of parts and the method.
Turn the ID into a number with int().

project_task.title: Game API
project_task.prompt:
Let's write the score API of Piko's Adventure. `handle(method, path, body=None)`:

- `GET /scores`: return the scores sorted from **highest to lowest**: `(200, list)`
- `POST /scores`: if `body` has `name` and `score`, add it and return `(201, new_entry)`; if something is missing, `(400, {"error": "missing information"})`
- Anything else: `(404, {"error": "no such path"})`
project_task.starter:
scores = [{"name": "Piko", "score": 300}, {"name": "Emma", "score": 450}]

def handle(method, path, body=None):
    pass

print(handle("GET", "/scores"))
print(handle("POST", "/scores", {"name": "Ben", "score": 120}))
hints: Check the path first: if path != "/scores":
For GET: sorted(scores, key=lambda s: s["score"], reverse=True)
For POST, first check whether information is missing.
